sites.name: Mt Kailash and Lake Manasarovar
sites.what: Sacred mountain and lake in western Tibet. India's MEA-run yatra (20 batches of 50 via Lipulekh and Nathu La in 2026) is for Indian pilgrims; Australians go through the Tibet permit and organised-tour route.

access.permits: Tibet Travel Permit through a China travel agent, organised tour only (see cn/tibet zone requirements); further area permits not yet checked

lore.text: Popular lore calls Kailash Mt Meru, the axis of the world, and a gateway to Shambhala.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source

sources.title: Launching of Kailash Manasarovar Yatra 2026
China travel advice

sites.name: Jokhang Temple Monastery, Lhasa
sites.what: Exceptional Buddhist religious complex, part of the Historic Ensemble of the Potala Palace (UNESCO).

access.permits: Tibet Entry Permit through a China travel agent, organised tour only (see zone requirements)

lore.text: Local legend says the Jokhang was built over a drained lake on the heart of a supine demoness.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source

sources.title: Historic Ensemble of the Potala Palace, Lhasa

sites.name: Guge Kingdom ruins and Tsaparang
sites.what: Ruined capital of the Guge kingdom in Zanda county, Ngari. The regional culture and tourism department announced on 29 September 2026 that the Guge cultural site park had reopened; keep to marked paths after snow.

access.permits: Tibet Travel Permit plus Ngari border and area permits through the tour agency (see zone requirements)
access.opening: Reopened late September 2026; hours not yet checked on an official page

lore.text: Popular lore claims Guge vanished almost overnight and that its people disappeared without trace.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source

sources.authority: Department of Culture and Tourism, Tibet Autonomous Region

sites.name: Piyang and Dungkar cave sites
sites.era: Buddhist cave temples of western Tibet
sites.what: Cave temples and the Dungkar Tashi Choling monastery ruins in Zanda county, listed by the State Council in 2013 as a major national heritage site; reopened with Guge in late September 2026.

access.permits: Tibet Travel Permit plus Ngari area permits through the tour agency

protection.law: Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level (7th batch, 2013)

sites.name: Samye Monastery
sites.what: In Samye town, Zhanang county, Shannan: described by the county government as Tibet's first monastery with all three jewels (Buddha, Dharma, Sangha), built in combined Tibetan, Han and Indian styles; a national protected site since 1996 and a 4A scenic area.

access.permits: Tibet Travel Permit through the tour agency

protection.law: Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level (4th batch, 1996)

lore.text: Local legend says Padmasambhava subdued the local spirits so the monastery could be built.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source

sources.title: 扎囊风景名胜：桑耶寺 (Samye Monastery)

sites.name: Pemako (Medog) hidden-land region
sites.what: Medog county's name Pemako (白玛岗) means 'hidden lotus'; the county government lists the Lotus Park and Monpa museum among its sights. Entry needs an electronic border management area pass applied for through the National Immigration Administration's 12367 app; the Zhamo road runs inbound on even dates and outbound on odd dates.

access.permits: Border area pass via the 12367 app (described for Chinese ID holders); whether foreign visitors can get one was not found on an official page
access.closures: Zhamo road alternates direction by date

lore.text: Popular lore and Tibetan Buddhist tradition call Pemako a beyul, a hidden land revealed to the worthy.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source

sources.title: 旅游温馨小贴士 (Travel tips)
进入墨脱前，这几件小事核对完再出发 (Before entering Medog)

sites.name: Bonri sacred mountain and Bon monasteries, Nyingchi
sites.what: Bonri mountain scenic area in Bayi district, Nyingchi, with the Bon monasteries Sejia Gengqin, Daze and Demu and the Demu cliff carvings; the district government reports plans for heritage protection and a cultural ecology protection area.

access.permits: Tibet Travel Permit through the tour agency

lore.text: Popular lore links Bon to the ancient Zhangzhung kingdom and to Mt Kailash as its holiest mountain.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source

ancient-sites-and-mysteries.summary: 7 site(s) in Tibet: Mt Kailash and Lake Manasarovar, Jokhang Temple Monastery, Lhasa, Guge Kingdom ruins and Tsaparang, Piyang and Dungkar cave sites, Samye Monastery, Pemako (Medog) hidden-land region, Bonri sacred mountain and Bon monasteries, Nyingchi. Facts from official sources; lore labelled as claims.
ancient-sites-and-mysteries.evidence: UNESCO pages and Smartraveller read directly; other official pages are search snapshots unless marked.

layers.process: Get permission from Chinese authorities and a Tibet Entry Permit from the Tibet Tourism Bureau. Applications go only through specialised travel agents in China, and you can only travel as part of an organised tour. Smartraveller says reconsider travel to Gyirong County (flooding, landslides) and exercise a high degree of caution in Tibet.

sources.supports: Tibet permit, organised-tour rule, advice levels (read directly). A Chinese government source is not yet found.

laws.rule: Foreign passport holders need a Tibet Travel Permit (入藏函) on top of a Chinese visa; it is applied for by a qualified Tibet travel agency, and foreigners must travel with that agency rather than independently. The permit is needed to board flights and trains into Tibet.

Visitors must keep to public order and manners, respect local customs, culture and religion, look after tourism resources, heritage and the environment, care for facilities, and cooperate with emergency limits on travel (article 13).
laws.penalty_signal: No fine on the visitor is set in the article read; breaches fall under the other laws that apply.
laws.heading: 西藏自治区旅游条例 (Tibet Autonomous Region Tourism Regulation)

laws.rule: Potala Palace heritage area: banned acts include pasting, carving or scribbling on heritage signs, climbing or crossing the relics and protective fittings, dumping or burning rubbish, damaging or occupying the buildings, putting up communications gear, ads or artificial sights, photographing where photography is banned, and bringing in flammable or dangerous items (article 12). Everyone entering must pass a security check and may not carry flammable, explosive, radioactive or corrosive items (article 19). Forging, altering or reselling Potala tickets is an offence (article 23).
laws.penalty_signal: Breaches of article 12 items 1 to 11: warning and possibly CNY 5,000 to 10,000 (about A$1,067 to A$2,133); CNY 30,000 to 50,000 (about A$6,400 to A$10,666) in serious cases, plus compensation for damage (article 30). Ticket resale: handled under the Public Security Administration Punishments Law (article 32). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
